newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian average lending rate 10.9 vs 12.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian average lending rate 10.9 vs 12.3 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate ended Tuesday weaker at 10.9 percent, compared with Monday's 12.3 percent, after slight cuts in term rates due to a further shrinking of demand for fresh kuna funds.
The money market trade fetched 37.5 million kuna, of which some 14 million were rolled over by creditors.
The main call money rate was steady at 10.5 percent save for savings banks, which paid 12 percent due to repayment risk.
Term rates for up to one-month borrowings ranged between 10.5-15 percent, charged by banks, and 9-12 percent for insurers' money.
The National Bank of Croatia granted some 30 million kuna Lombard funds at 9.5 percent to one commercial bank.
It calculated the kuna midrates for Wednesday's dealings weaker at 6.2002 versus 6.1944 to the dollar and 3.5796 versus 3.5756 against the German mark.
The midrates are an average of commercial banks' sell rates in the previous day's trade. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
